content.text:
**Answer: KRuO4 (mp-14005) alone.**

- **Main observed peaks:** about 16.8° (38), 25.25° (100, broad), 26.7° (15), 31.25° (22) and about 35.1° (9). I located the later peaks by counting grid points, so their positions are approximate.
- **KRuO4 cell:** I converted the body-centred primitive cell (a_p = 7.712 Å) to the conventional cell. That gives a ≈ 5.76 Å and c ≈ 13.1 Å.
- **KRuO4 predicted peaks:**
  - (101) at about 16.8°, matching the 16.8° peak.
  - (103) and (112) at about 25.6–25.7°. These would merge into the strong, broad peak near 25.3°, though they sit about 0.3–0.4° high.
  - (004) at about 27.2°, close to the 26.7° peak.
  - (200) at about 31.0°, close to 31.25°.
- **Why not anatase TiO2:** its strongest line (101, about 25.3°) also fits the main peak. However, anatase has no reflection near 16.8°, so it cannot account for that peak.
- **Other candidates:** I did not compute patterns for the other seven. The four peak groups I matched all fit KRuO4, so I see no need for a second phase.

{"present": ["mp-14005"], "confidence": 0.75, "note": "The 16.8° peak matches KRuO4 (101) and the strong broad 25.3° peak fits its merged (103)/(112) lines, which anatase cannot fully explain since it has no line near 16.8°."}
